concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy showed a dense acute neutrophilic infiltrate extending into adipose tissue and septa, consistent with neutrophilic panniculitis.
The patient has a history of sickle cell disease and presented with symptoms consistent with a sickle cell crisis, including severe abdominal pain and bloody stools.
The patient has a history of ulcerative colitis and presented with symptoms consistent with a flare, including bloody stools and abdominal pain.
The patient has a history of autoimmune hepatitis and presented with elevated C-reactive protein levels, consistent with an autoimmune hepatitis flare.
The patient presented with symptoms consistent with vasculitis, including hemorrhagic vesicles and a tender, swollen knee.
The patient has a history of ulcerative colitis and presented with symptoms consistent with inflammatory bowel disease.
The patient has a history of sickle cell disease and presented with anemia, consistent with hemolytic anemia.
The patient presented with elevated C-reactive protein levels and leukocytosis, consistent with systemic inflammation.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of intermittent fever, severe intermittent abdominal pain, and bloody stools, along with laboratory findings of leukocytosis and anemia, support systemic inflammation as the most comprehensive explanation for the clinical presentation.
